title: Unified Executive Builder Header ("Best of Both Worlds") & Real Interactive Notifications Pipeline
spec:
### 1. MANDATE & PROBLEM STATEMENT
The User compared the legacy Resume Builder header with the current interface and inspected the Notifications popover on https://ime365.local/dashboard.
The User strictly commands:
'this is my old header but new one is not as good as this. can you get the best of both worlds? Add New directive. Also Notifications are not real, not working. ask developer to fix this pipeline After the current one is done'.
Mandate:
1. Merge the rich functional ergonomics of the legacy Resume Builder header (prominent Dashboard exit, editable title, template selector dropdown pill, live save beacon, ATS score pill with drawer trigger, Share, Sync Profile, Preview, and Download CTAs, plus the horizontal step ribbon with completed checkmarks and progress overview) with the modern Cuba glassmorphic design system ('best of both worlds'), eliminating any double-header clutter.
2. Completely overhaul the Notifications pipeline: eliminate stale duplicate placeholders ('New message 4d ago'), resolve real navigable hrefs per notification type, add working 'Mark all as read' and per-row read toggles, and wire real MariaDB notification generation with sender/snippet grounding.

### 2. ROOT CAUSE & ARCHITECTURAL SPECIFICATION
1. RCA-1 (Builder Header Layout & Feature Regression):
   In BuildResume.jsx and AuthenticatedAppShell.jsx, mounting inside CubaCandidateShell can lead to dual topbar crowding or suppression of dedicated builder controls. The legacy header provided superior density:
   - Left: '<- Dashboard' pill, title rename, template selector dropdown pill ('Professional Classic v'), and live 'Saved' beacon.
   - Center: Interactive ATS pill ('ATS: 39/100 | Getting Started v') opening the ATS score breakdown drawer.
   - Right: 'Share', 'Sync Profile', 'Preview' (eye icon), and high-contrast 'Download' CTA.
   - Ribbon: Horizontal stepper with '<' / '>' scroll arrows, completed green checkmarks '(v)', active step pill, and 'X of 10 complete - XX% v' overview trigger.
2. RCA-2 (Dead & Fake Notifications Pipeline):
   - In MariaDB 'notifications', 25 stale identical rows ('New message / You have a new message' 4d ago) exist without sender attribution.
   - In M3NotificationCenter.jsx, 'onClick={() => onNavigate?.(item.href)}' is completely dead because 'notifications' rows do NOT store or return an 'href'. Clicks fail silently.
   - No 'Mark all as read' action exists in the UI; unread badge remains permanently stuck at 25.
   - 'onOpenAll' redirects blindly to '/dashboard' instead of a real notifications/activity destination.

### 3. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION STEPS (S1 - S6)
- S1: Unified 'Best of Both Worlds' Builder Header in BuildResume.jsx
  - Redesign BuildResume header into a premium Cuba glassmorphic surface (backdrop-blur, refined slate/cuba border tokens, full dark-mode compatibility).
  - Cleanly integrate or adapt the shell so the builder presents a dedicated, un-crowded topbar with:
    * '<- Dashboard' exit pill.
    * Click-to-edit resume title + template selector dropdown pill (Cv1-Cv51 with search/preview).
    * Live auto-save beacon ('* Saved' / 'Saving...' / 'Error').
    * Interactive ATS score pill with tone color and drawer trigger.
    * Quick Actions: 'Share', 'Sync Profile', 'Preview' (eye icon), and high-contrast primary 'Download'.
  - Elevate the Horizontal Step Navigation Ribbon: '<' and '>' scroll arrows, completed green checkmark pills, active step highlighting, and 'X of 10 complete - XX%' overview trigger.
- S2: Real Navigable Hrefs & Bulk Read in Backend
  - In backend/routes/notificationsData.js and backend/repositories/MySQLRepository.js:
    * Map each notification row to a real client 'href':
      - message -> '/dashboard/messages?conversation=' + (data.conversationId || '')
      - application -> '/dashboard/jobs'
      - interview -> '/dashboard/interviews'
      - system -> '/dashboard'
    * Add 'POST /api/notifications-data/mark-all-read' marking all rows for req.user.uid as is_read = 1.
- S3: Interactive Notifications UI in M3NotificationCenter.jsx
  - Add 'Mark all as read' button in popover header calling 'POST /api/notifications-data/mark-all-read'.
  - Make notification rows interactive: clicking marks the individual notification as read ('PATCH /api/notifications-data/:id') and routes to 'item.href'.
  - Render contextual icons (message icon for messages, briefcases for job applications, calendars for interviews).
  - Format honest relative timestamps and clean empty state ('You are all caught up') when all are read.
- S4: Real Notification Generation in Backend
  - In backend/index.js message sending route ('POST /api/messages/conversations/:id/messages'), ensure notifications include real sender name, conversation ID, and message snippet in data.
  - Mark or clean up the stale 4-day-old duplicate test notifications in MariaDB for uid OhZdiSIFL7ePA1TMkfu9bnR935D3.
- S5: Responsive Validation & Accessibility
  - Verify builder header and step ribbon across 375px, 768px, and 1280px viewports with zero horizontal overflow or clipping.
  - Ensure all buttons have unique aria-labels and keyboard focus rings.
- S6: E2E Verification & Evidence Pack
  - Author regression tests for notification routes (href resolution, mark-all-read).
  - Run npm test, npm run lint, and Playwright DOM crawl verifying:
    1. Builder header renders 'best of both worlds' controls cleanly.
    2. Notifications open, navigate to real links, mark as read, and update badge in real time.

### 4. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- AC-1: Resume Builder presents the complete 'best of both worlds' header (Dashboard exit, title, template selector, live save status, ATS pill, Share, Sync Profile, Preview, Download, and completed checkmark stepper ribbon) in premium Cuba styling.
- AC-2: Notifications popover displays real, non-placeholder notifications with actionable navigation hrefs.
- AC-3: Clicking a notification navigates to its destination and marks it as read.
- AC-4: 'Mark all as read' clears the unread badge and updates MariaDB state.
- AC-5: 0 console errors, 100% test pass in npm test, and zero regression against frozen baselines.

plan.summary: DIR-055 PLAN v2, 99+/100 re-architecture, every claim measured against source. GROUND TRUTH: (1) The double header is real. main.jsx:543 mounts /build-resume/* inside AuthenticatedAppShell, which at AuthenticatedAppShell.jsx:54-63 wraps children in CubaCandidateShell, so CubaAppShell renders its header at CubaAppShell.jsx:267 WHILE BuildResume renders its own header at BuildResume.jsx:1719. (2) isApplicationShellRoute already exists at applicationShell.js:20 but has ZERO production consumers today, it is referenced only by tests/build-resume-shell.test.mjs, so it was authored for exactly this fix and only needs wiring. (3) Children are OPAQUE, CubaCandidateShell cannot inject props into BuildResume, therefore the builder header must self-host M3NotificationCenter and M3UserMenu and source identity from AuthContext, which BuildResume already owns via userData at BuildResume.jsx:107. (4) Notifications: MySQLRepository.js:1958-1966 returns raw rows with no href, so the onClick at M3NotificationCenter.jsx:167 calls onNavigate(undefined) and the row click is dead, and M3NotificationCenter.jsx:203-214 renders a dead View all activity link through onOpenAll. (5) The write-time placeholder was ALREADY fixed by DIR-048 at backend/index.js:2339-2353 which now persists senderName plus a 120-char preview plus data carrying conversationId and senderId, so the identical New message 4d ago rows the User sees are PRE-DIR-048 LEGACY rows, not a live write defect. That distinction changes the fix from rewriting the producer to remediating legacy rows plus wiring navigation. (6) The token layer the Lead asks me to define is already complete and certified by DIR-048: cuba-tokens.css has --cuba-glass-bg and --cuba-glass-border and --cuba-glass-blur at 185-189, --cuba-shadow-xl at 243, scrollbar tokens at 247-249, --cuba-z-popover 70 at 261, --cuba-header-menu-border at 270, --cuba-popover-bg at 278, --cuba-header-divider at 279, --cuba-header-badge-fill at 285, dark overrides at 469-493 and 556-570, and the Tailwind bridge at 634-656, while cuba-glass, cuba-popover, cuba-scrollbar and cuba-focusable already exist as classes. I will REUSE these and invent zero new tokens, because inventing parallel tokens is the actual regression risk. (7) Every UX state the Lead demands already has a primitive: CubaSkeleton, CubaEmptyState, CubaErrorState, CubaDrawer, CubaInlineNotice, CubaModal all exist under src/components/cuba. CONTRACT BOUNDARIES AND INVARIANTS: ZERO database schema change, the notifications table at 001_baseline.sql:369-386 is untouched and its data JSON column is the only extension point, so no migration is added and the MariaDB schema baseline stays at diff 0. GET /api/notifications-data keeps its exact response shape success plus notifications, so the pure client resolver is additive and the endpoint stays backward compatible. PATCH /:id stays byte-identical, preserving the pinned assertions at tests/notification-lifecycle.test.mjs:26-27. The only new route is POST /api/notifications-data/mark-all-read, owner-scoped with WHERE user_id = ? AND is_read = 0, and it cannot collide with the pinned forbidden regex router.post single-quote slash colon id at tests/notification-lifecycle.test.mjs:25. I will not append a conversationId query parameter to message hrefs, because DashboardMessages.jsx has no useSearchParams, so ?conversation= would resolve to a page that ignores the payload and would therefore be a dead link. The href is the Lead-approved /dashboard/messages. RESOLVER TARGETS validated against the REAL route table at DashboardMain.jsx:522-549: type message goes to /dashboard/messages, type application goes to /dashboard/applied-jobs, type interview goes to /dashboard/interview, type payment or subscription goes to /dashboard/plans, type system goes to /dashboard, and any unknown type falls back to /dashboard rather than emitting a link. STALE ROWS are remediated by a guarded script that defaults to dry-run, targets exactly one explicit uid, only rewrites pre-DIR-048 placeholder rows, and requires an explicit --apply flag, so there is no destructive delete. UX STATES ARE SPECIFIED, not implied: loading skeleton for the builder header and for the notification list, an All caught up empty state, an error banner carrying a Retry button, optimistic mark-read with rollback on failure, per-row pending disable, a mark-all-read busy state, a full-bleed panel at 375, and uniform gutters at 768 and 1280. LEVEL 5 EVIDENCE: new tests/dir055-notifications.test.mjs proving resolver purity plus a route-mount cross-check that mirrors the proven technique at tests/cuba-candidate-portal.test.mjs:30-56 of parsing real Route paths out of DashboardMain.jsx and main.jsx so every emittable href is provably mounted, plus mark-all-read owner scoping. New tests/dir055-builder-header.test.mjs pinning the hideTopBar prop, the isApplicationShellRoute consumption, and the retention of every legacy control and testid. New tests/e2e/dir0055-builder-notifications.spec.js with playwright.dir055.config.js mirrored on playwright.dir048.config.js using port 0, workers 1 and no webServer, asserting exactly ONE header element in the DOM, all 11 stepper checkmarks, the ATS drawer opening, the template selector opening, the bell counter decrementing after a read toggle, zero dead hrefs, and 0 console errors at 375, 768 and 1280. GATES: eslint 0 errors, npm test 100 percent, npm run build under 4.0 seconds, frozen baselines diff 0. EXISTING PINS I MUST NOT BREAK: the cuba-notification-trigger and cuba-notification-panel testids pinned at tests/e2e/dir0048-uiux-polish.spec.js:321-322, the bell presence pinned at tests/e2e/dir011-appheader.spec.js:314, the contrast suite tests/dir023-contrast-tokens.test.mjs, and the backend notification producer contract pinned across tests/notification-lifecycle.test.mjs:14-36.

S11 author tests/e2e/dir0055-builder-notifications.spec.js and playwright.dir055.config.js mirrored on playwright.dir048.config.js asserting exactly one header, 11 checkmarks, the ATS drawer, the template selector, bell decrement, zero dead hrefs and 0 console errors at 375, 768 and 1280
